item.title: Pakistan's WTC revival needs a major rethink! Bowling coach Shaun Tait hints at the way forward
item.description: Pakistan fast bowling coach Shaun Tait believes a significant change in the country's home conditions could hold the key to making the side more competitive in the World Test Championship (WTC) in the coming years. Tait has backed the preparation of seamer-friendly pitches in Pakistan, arguing that such surfaces could help the team build a stronger fast-bowling attack and improve its prospects in the longest format. “These sort of (greenish) wickets going forward for Pakistan cricket, I believe personally is the way forward,” Tait told reporters on Monday after overseeing the fast bowlers during the final two-hour net session ahead of Tuesday's second Test against Sri Lanka. Pakistan drew the opening Test at Rawalpindi after rain and bad light resulted in at least 141 overs being lost. The match was played on a grassy surface, where 31-year-old pacer Saqib Khan made an impressive debut, claiming seven wickets. Pakistan have prepared another greenish pitch for the second Test, which was shifted from Lahore to Rawalpindi after smog levels increased in the provincial capital. “It looks similar to the last (test) pitch,” Tait said. “But again, like with the grass lengths and stuff, I’m not good with that sort of thing, but it looks like there’s some grass coverage, which is always a good sign.” Saqib's breakthrough offers Pakistan encouragement Saqib was the standout performer in the opening Test, taking 7/130 in Sri Lanka's first innings to restrict their lead to just 12 runs. His spell came under favourable overcast conditions after Kusal Mendis and Dhananjaya de Silva had dominated the third day with a 249-run partnership. The fast bowler had already taken 81 wickets in 19 first-class matches over the previous four domestic seasons before earning his Test opportunity. Tait was particularly impressed by his ability to use the new ball. “He (Saqib) did a really good job, especially with the new ball,” Tait said. “Obviously he’s played quite a bit of first-class cricket, which is great … he’s got experience behind him in Pakistan, so that was really helpful to be able to bring in a player that had played enough first-class cricket and taken wickets.” Saqib was among four successful Pakistan debutants in the first Test, with Tayyab Arif, Mohammad Taha and Arafat Minhas scoring half-centuries. Pakistan looking to rebuild after difficult WTC campaign Pakistan entered the Sri Lanka series at the bottom of the WTC standings after winning only two and losing seven Tests in the cycle. Babar Azam continued his search for a first Test century since December 2022, with his drought extending to 42 innings. Saud Shakeel also narrowly missed a century in both innings, scoring 97 in the second to help Pakistan hold on for the draw. With another green surface prepared in Rawalpindi, Pakistan will hope their fast bowlers can again make an impact as they look to build a more competitive Test side.

item.title: The Viva El Birdos Podcast: Episode 91 – Interview with Eno Sarris
item.description: Diving Deep into Cardinals Pitching Options with Eno Sarris Insights and evaluations from the AFL Championship and free agency Welcome back to the Viva El Birdos Podcast! This week, host Jake Wood is joined by Eno Sarris, co-host of the Rates and Barrels podcast and a writer for The Athletic . They dive into some critical evaluations of the Cardinals’ prospects and potential offseason moves. AFL Insights Eno recently attended the Arizona Fall League (AFL), where he got a firsthand look at several Cardinals prospects. He noted that this league isn’t known for strong pitching, as many top pitchers don’t participate due to fatigue from the season. However, he shared some promising observations about Cardinals players: “Roby looks pretty good. His slider and changeup are plus pitches by the model. He commands them well and they’re plus by stuff.” Eno highlighted that while many pitchers in the AFL struggle, Roby stands out with a solid five-pitch mix. However, he cautioned that other pitchers like Ellisalt and King showed mixed results, with only one standout pitch each. Free Agent Market Analysis As the offseason approaches, Jake and Eno discuss potential free-agent targets for the Cardinals. Eno emphasizes the need for pitchers with strong stuff: “The market is pretty rough. There are like four or five guys who have above-average stuff, and half of them are injured.” He mentioned names like Patrick Sandoval and Nick Pivetta as intriguing possibilities, suggesting Sandoval could be a good fit given his potential upside and the chance for a bounce-back season. Evaluating Casey Mize Another topic of discussion was Casey Mize, a pitcher who struggled after moving to San Diego. Eno expressed skepticism about Mize’s ability to regain his form, noting: “He has a reverse split problem. I’m not sure that I see a solution going forward.” Despite Mize’s past success, Eno pointed out that he might be looking for a multi-year deal, making him a less likely fit for the Cardinals. Third Base Dilemma Finally, they touched on the Cardinals’ third-base situation. Eno provided a balanced view on Blaze Jordan’s prospects: “If you prorate Blaze Jordan’s projections, you get just around the league average guy. I really like his bat speed, but I do not like his plate approach at all.” As the conversation unfolded, they explored whether the Cardinals should seek a more established player at third base or trust in Jordan’s development. With plenty of insights and evaluations to digest, this episode offers a deep dive into the future of the Cardinals. For a more detailed discussion, be sure to check out the full episode! item.title: Michigan Football plummets in ESPN’s SP+ rankings after Oregon loss
item.description: EUGENE, OR - NOVEMBER 14: Andrew Marsh #3 of the Michigan Wolverines catches a pass during the 1st half of a game between the Michigan Wolverines and Oregon Ducks at Autzen Stadium on November 14, 2026 in Eugene, Oregon. (Photo by Al Sermeno/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images) | ISI Photos via Getty Images Michigan is a .500 football team after losing its latest game to Oregon on Saturday, a 31-7 thumping in which the defensive dam that’s been sturdy all season finally broke. With the loss, Michigan once again finds itself falling in ESPN and Bill Connelly’s SP+ rankings. The Wolverines are now down to No. 43 in the country, a seven-spot drop from last week. For those of you who might be new to SP+, it’s an advanced metric that takes into account a team’s offensive, defensive, and special teams efficiencies. It combines all three metrics into one uniform metric that predicts how many points a given team would defeat (or lose to) the “average” college football team by on a neutral field. In other words, it’s a metric designed to look at how “good” teams really are at different aspects of the game rather than ranking them purely on their resumes. In Michigan’s case, its rating is 7.0 after Week 11, meaning it would beat an “average” college football team by 7.0 points on a neutral field. Looking closer at each side of the ball, SP+ gives the Wolverines the No. 104-ranked offense, No. 7-ranked defense (which understandably took a bit of a drop with its worst statistical outing of the season), and No. 128-ranked special teams units – unsurprising figures based on what we’ve seen in ten games this year. The Wolverines still have two games left in the regular season, both of which are against teams that are down to their backup quarterbacks in UCLA and Ohio State. Both teams are ranked higher than Michigan on SP+ (and every advanced metric, for that matter), so Michigan is projected to lose both games and finish the season 5-7. UCLA will be the opponent in the final home game of the season. The Bruins are undefeated and have had a total revival under first-year head coach Bob Chesney, with their big strength being their defense, which is No. 3 in the country on SP+. They enter this matchup at No. 12 in the rankings with a rating of 21.1, meaning they are predicted to defeat Michigan by about 14.1 points despite many sportsbooks predicting a one-possession game.

item.title: Dana White recounts ‘crazy’ and ‘unique’ experience being nominated as press secretary for President Donald Trump
item.description: WASHINGTON, DC - NOVEMBER 09: Ultimate Fighting Championship CEO Dana White speaks as U.S. President Donald Trump looks on in the James S. Brady Press Briefing Room of the White House on November 09, 2026 in Washington, DC. (Photo by Chip Somodevilla/Getty Images) | Getty Images Dana White was at a Zuffa Boxing event in London when his world was suddenly turned upside down after President Donald Trump dropped a message that the UFC CEO was being nominated to take over as the press secretary for his office. At the time, White had no idea what was exactly happening but Trump’s message on Truth Social became a massive story even if the job offer wasn’t exactly genuine. Trump would late say he was just “kidding” but that didn’t stop the news from exploding on a global scale and what may have started as a joke suddenly became national news. “I was in London at a fight and he called me and was basically like ‘hey, I told the press that you’re going to be the next press secretary,’” White recounted when speaking to Fox News. “He was laughing and I hadn’t really thought about what that would be like. An hour later, my guy Hunter [Campbell], who is my right hand man at the UFC calls me and says ‘this is the biggest story in America right now, this is everywhere.’ Then Lenee [Breckenridge], my head of PR, was just like ‘every news outlet in the world is calling right now.’ “I was supposed to fly to D.C. right after the fight. I’ve got a house in Maine so I just flew to my house in Maine. Hid out for 24 hours and flew to D.C. on Monday. You saw how the rest played out.” White eventually made his way to Washington D.C. to meet with the president and he actually appeared at a White House press briefing but ultimately turned down the half-hearted job offer. While he didn’t become press secretary, White did get to answer some questions during the briefing and even that experience was surreal for him. “It was incredible,” White said. “What an amazing experience. Literally when I was pulling into the gates of the White House, his assistant called and said ‘we’re going to take you right down to the press room, he wants you now.’ I was like what? This is crazy. It was a very unique and crazy 48 hours for me.” White has welcomed Trump to numerous UFC events and their friendship has obviously taken center stage during both of his times in office. Nearly taking over as press secretary — even in jest — might end up at the top of the list for White’s experiences since knowing Trump. “Another one of one experience for me,” White said. “Being friends with him, these crazy things that have happened in my life. It was a very, very cool experience.”

item.title: How Andy Robertson defied the odds to become Scotland’s greatest captain
item.description: It was a burst from the left wing that would be seen time and time again. Andy Robertson ’s first goal for Scotland came on just his fourth appearance for his country, at 20 years old and only a few months after completing a £2.85m move from Dundee United to Hull City. The wider importance of the goal was ultimately forgotten, a late consolation against England in a 3-1 defeat at Celtic Park. But for Robertson, with his wide-eyed excitement and the determination to carry his run forward, it was the moment that set the tone for what was to follow. Twelve years later, Robertson has overtaken the great Sir Kenny Dalglish to become the most-capped Scotland’s men’s player of all time, passing his hero and legend for both his childhood club, Celtic , and adopted one, Liverpool , with his 103rd international appearance against Switzerland. It is only in keeping with Robertson’s humility that he was the first to insist Dalglish remains Scotland’s greatest player ; it is only in keeping with Dalglish’s typical wry humour that he reminds Robertson that his own tally of international appearances would be much higher had competitions like the Nations League been around in his day. “It’s not really about me,” Robertson said ahead of taking the record. "It’s about him [Dalglish] in my opinion. For how long the record stood, for what he achieved in his career, for the person he is.” Andy Robertson has overtaken Kenny Dalglish to become Scotland's most capped player (PA) But Scotland will celebrate Robertson, too. What is not up for debate is the scale of achievement and the remarkable nature of his journey. His story is well known yet will be retold many times this week: how a boy released by Celtic for being too small and who worked in the Hampden ticket office while playing part-time with Queen’s Park would become one of the world’s best left-backs and a Champions League and Premier League winner. With Scotland, part of Robertson’s legacy is formed by qualifying for three major tournaments in five years, when the Tartan Army had not previously been on the big stage since 1998. Robertson was the leader on each campaign under Steve Clarke, from the penalties against Serbia to reach Euro 2020 to beating Spain and Norway to deservedly make Euro 2024. Then, in the delirium that was Scotland’s win over Denmark to qualify for the World Cup, it was Robertson who provided another moment of inspiration when he poignantly remembered his late friend Diogo Jota and the promise they had made to each other while watching the 2022 World Cup four years before. Robertson has led his nation with dignity and class and if insists that Dalglish remains the King, the counter is to suggest that he stands, by some way, as Scotland’s greatest captain. He has worn the armband 80 times, with an 81st cap as skipper to come in St Gallen, putting him well clear of George Young, on 48, and Billie Bremner, on 39. item.description: LYNCHBURG, VA - OCTOBER 08: Liberty Flames quarterback Deshawn Purdie (5) accelerates upfield during a college football game between the Sam Houston Bearkats and the Liberty Flames on October 8, 2026, at Williams Stadium in Lynchburg, VA. (Photo by Lee Coleman/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images For the first time since 2023, Conference USA has made a splash in the AP Poll. The Liberty Flames (9-1, 6-0 CUSA) checked in at No. 22 in the rankings released Monday. Liberty is the first CUSA program ranked since 2023, when it finished No. 25, produced a 13-1 record, won the CUSA championship, and qualified for the Fiesta Bowl. 2026 represents the fourth season in the last six years where Liberty appeared in the AP Poll. The Flames held rankings in 2020 and 2022 under former head coach Hugh Freeze, while current head coach Jamey Chadwell cracked the Top 25 in 2023 and this season. Chadwell has led the Flames to nine consecutive wins, including seven by double-digits. Liberty’s lone defeat came in Week 1 at James Madison where they fell 20-13. Since, both sides of the ball have clicked, and the Flames rank fourth in scoring margin against FBS opponents (+20.2 per game), 31st in scoring offense (32.8 points per game), and eighth in scoring defense (14.5 points allowed per game). The Flames have not surrendered more than 23 points in a single game all season and have taken exceptional care of the ball, throwing just one interception and boasting a plus-8 in the turnover battle. Liberty is one 10 FBS teams with one loss or fewer heading into Week 12, and its nine-game win streak is tied with Boise State for the third-longest in the country, only trailing Utah (16) and UCLA (10). Liberty’s remaining schedule includes a Week 12 home matchup against Western Kentucky and a Week 13 road trip to Missouri State. Both opponents are on the brink of being eliminated from bowl eligibility, sporting 4-6 overall records and 3-3 marks in the CUSA standings. The Flames have already secured a spot in the 2026 CUSA Championship Game, which will kick off on Friday, Dec. 4. The host site and opponent are not official yet. Jacksonville State is one win away from securing a spot as Liberty’s opponent in the title game. The Flames can clinch hosting privileges this weekend with one more win combined with a Jacksonville State loss. item.title: George Pickens Joins Cowboys Legends With Historic 3-TD Night
item.description: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images George Pickens did not just play well on Sunday; he rewrote the Dallas Cowboys history books. The former Hoover standout put up numbers that belong in the same sentence as franchise icons. This was a bounce-back show after missing the previous week against the Indianapolis Colts due to injury. The 25-year-old wide receiver was seemingly unstoppable against a tough San Francisco 49ers defense, per RotoBaller. RotoWire reports that he secured 11 of 18 targets for 145 yards and three touchdowns during the defeat. The stats are undeniable, even if the final score did not go Dallas’s way. Legends Only Pickens has now joined a very small, very exclusive club in Cowboys history. Terrell Owens and Bob Hayes are the only other Cowboys receivers to reach 2,000 yards in their first 26 games, a milestone he achieved according to AL.com. That is a level of production that separates great players from franchise pillars. It shows he can dominate the field and move the chains when the team needs him most. RotoBaller notes that this output established a new season peak for Pickens in both receptions and yardage. RotoWire states that he caught 11 of 18 targets for 145 yards and three touchdowns in Sunday’s 46-40 Cowboys loss to the 49ers. The offense could not stop him, but the defense ultimately could not stop San Francisco either. Winning Still Matters Stat lines look great on paper, but the Cowboys need wins to make the playoffs. RotoBaller adds that while Pickens reached the end zone, it unfortunately failed to secure victory for his squad. Individual brilliance does not fix a broken defense or a coaching mistake. Fans want to see the best player on the field, but they want to see that player on the winning side. The next game is Sunday, Nov. 22, at 1 p.m. ET against the Tennessee Titans at AT&T Stadium.

item.title: Rutgers men’s soccer earns NCAA Tournament bid
item.description: After a fall full of upset wins, the Rutgers men’s soccer team has earned a chance to make a run toward a national championship. The Scarlet Knights earned their first bid to the NCAA Tournament since 2022 (and their first at-large bid since 2015), notching the third seed in the Georgetown regional of the 48-team field, according to the NCAA’s selection show on Monday. Rutgers will have first-round bye before hosting a home game in the second round. The Scarlet Knights will welcome the winner of Thursday’s match between Cornell and Fairleigh Dickinson on Sunday at 6 p.m. to Yurcak Field. It will mark the first NCAA Tournament game hosted by the Scarlet Knights since 2015, when the Scarlet Knights defeated LIU Brooklyn in a penalty shootout after a 1-1 draw through regulation and extra time. JOIN OUR RUTGERS RANT DISCORD: Talk Rutgers with Steve Politi, Brian Fonseca . Rutgers (9-6-3) earned their spot in the postseason after a standout campaign that featured six wins over ranked opponents. MORE BY BRIAN FONSECA Kickoff time for Rutgers football’s final home game of 2026 against Michigan State set Nov. 16, 2026, 1:11 p.m. Can Rutgers realistically turn bleak outlook under Greg Schiano around in one offseason? | Rutgers Rant Nov. 16, 2026, 11:43 a.m. The Scarlet Knights defeated three ranked foes in a row in mid-September, upsetting No. 11 UCLA, No. 11 Princeton and No. 3 Ohio State in the span of a week. Of Rutgers’ six losses, four came to ranked opponents: No. 5 Georgetown, No. 21 UC Santa Barbara, No. 7 Maryland and No. 20 Wisconsin. item.title: Titans changed their offensive philosophy after Colts game
item.description: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - NOVEMBER 15: Cam Ward #1 of the Tennessee Titans reacts during the first half against the Jacksonville Jaguars at Nissan Stadium on November 15, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Justin Ford/Getty Images) | Getty Images Robert Saleh said at his Monday press conference this morning that the Tennessee Titans changed their offensive philosophy after the game against the Indianapolis Colts. You can see the whole answer here: Titans HC Robert Saleh’s full response this morning on changing the team’s philosophical approach to the offense around Cam Ward a few weeks ago (via @Titans ) pic.twitter.com/GwxUG4z1k4 — Buck Reising (@BuckReising) November 16, 2026 The changes they have made have certainly paid off. The Titans are averaging almost 28 points per game in that span. Cam Ward has looked much more comfortable. He wasn’t that good in the loss to the Cleveland Browns, which was the first game they made the switch, but he has been really good since. There are probably a couple of reasons they made the switch. The first is that running the offense up-tempo benefits Ward because it fits his style of play. He is better out of structure than in structure. You can’t always play out of structure as an NFL quarterback, but it makes sense to create more of those opportunities. The other reason is that the defense, which was already bad, lost its two best players over that span. If the Titans are going to have any chance to win games, they are going to have to score a bunch of points. It is going to take another 30-point effort for them to have a chance against the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday. I wrote early on this season that Brian Daboll needed to open things up for Ward. The conservative offense just wasn’t working. It is good to see that they made the decision in-house to do that. Hopefully, it will eventually lead to some wins.

item.title: Hornets Score 11 Points Fewer Than Opponents In Early Season Slump
item.description: Kiyoshi Mio-Imagn Images The Charlotte Hornets are losing the scoring battle by a wide margin. The team averages 98.6 points per game while their opponents put up 109.6. This 11-point gap shows up clearly in the stats from the first 12 games. The Hornets have shot just .401 from the field during this stretch. Their opponents shot a much better .470. That difference in shooting accuracy tells the whole story of why the score keeps getting away from Charlotte. Miller Carries the Load Alone One player is doing the heavy lifting for the offense. Miller played 10 games and averaged 20.6 points per outing. He shot .356 from the field while playing 31 minutes a night. No other player on the roster comes close to that number. Reid played 12 games and scored 17.3 points per game, which is the second-best mark. Allen played 12 games too and added 15.2 points. The rest of the team struggles to find the net in a big way. Williams played just one game but still managed 11 points on .600 shooting. Schröder played 9 games and averaged 10.2 points. White played 5 games and scored 9.8 points. The drop-off after the top three is steep. Diabaté played 10 games and averaged 8.7 points, Salaün appeared in 11 games with 6.5 points, and James played 12 games, averaging 6.0 points. item.title: Former delivery driver Dean earns PGA Tour card
item.description: Joe Dean won the British Masters in August [Getty Images] Former supermarket delivery driver Joe Dean has continued a whirlwind year by earning a place on the PGA Tour. Englishman Dean, 32, was ranked 2,930th in the world rankings two years ago as he worked part time to help fund his golf career. In July he earned a place at The Open after winning the inaugural Last-Chance Qualifier, but things really took off for him in August when he claimed the British Masters title - his first DP World Tour win in his 70th event. He finished tied for 27th place at the season-ending World Tour Championship on Sunday, which meant he secured enough points in the Race to Dubai rankings to secure his PGA Tour card and ensure he can compete for more lucrative prize money. He almost missed out, as his final round two-over-par 74 meant he dropped out of the qualification spots, but a last-hole bogey by Mikael Lindberg moved Dean back into the 10th and final qualifying place. Dean's British Masters win saw him claim £440,000 in prize money, more than he had earned in total from his previous 19 tournaments in the 2026 season. Despite his impressive rise over the last year, Dean recently said in an interview with Today's Golfer than he can find the sport stressful. "A lot of people are probably going to hate me for saying this, but if I could earn a better living doing something else, I probably would," he said. "Even in the moment when I'm playing well, it's not fun. It's stressful. There's a ton of pressure and I don't find that fun. I find being sat by a fishing lake or cleaning my car fun and no pressure. But that's just personal to me." Meanwhile, 2018 US Masters champion Patrick Reed secured his return to the PGA Tour four years after departing for LIV Golf. The 36-year-old American left LIV Golf at the start of this year to play on the DP World Tour. He then won two tournaments early on to earn one of the 10 PGA Tour cards through the European circuit.

item.title: Mahomes And Rice Prove Deep Ball Trust Is Alive In Kansas City
item.description: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images Patrick Mahomes threw a long pass on Sunday afternoon and sent a clear message to the defense that the deep ball is still part of the plan. The connection with Rashee Rice for 50 yards was not a lucky break or a fluke play that happened by mistake. It was a calculated strike that shows the quarterback still trusts his young receiver to make the catch and run after it. A Strike That Changes the Game The 50-yard gain forced the Atlanta Falcons to respect the vertical threat deep down the field. Before this play, the defense might have thought they could crowd the line of scrimmage without fear. Mahomes proved them wrong by launching the ball with precision and Rice proved his worth by catching it in stride. The deep ball opens up the entire field for the rest of the offense. When a team has to worry about the deep ball, it creates space for the short passes and the running game to work much better. The Kansas City Chiefs highlighted this moment as a can’t-miss play that defined the flow of the game. The Falcons had a solid defense, yet they could not stop the connection when it mattered most. This success shows that the chemistry between Mahomes and Rice is growing stronger every week. They do not need a lot of time or a perfect setup to make it happen. They just need one look, and the ball is in the air before the defense can react. The ability to go deep changes how teams prepare for the Chiefs in the weeks ahead. Opponents cannot just play safe; they have to send safeties back, which leaves holes in the middle of the field. This dynamic was on full display during the 35-13 win over Atlanta. Chiefs fans know that Mahomes can make every throw, but seeing him hit a receiver like Rice on a 50-yard bomb confirms that the team has a reliable weapon outside. This play is a sign of what the offense can do when everything clicks. The passing game moves the chains and breaks the game open. The trust between the two is the foundation for this kind of explosive play. The team now turns its attention to the next matchup on the schedule. The Arizona Cardinals will come to Arrowhead Stadium on Sunday, Nov. 22, for a 1 p.m. ET kickoff. This upcoming game will test if the deep ball success against Atlanta was a one-time event or a new standard for the season. The defense will try to stop the run first, but the threat of the deep pass remains a constant danger. The Chiefs have shown they can score in many ways, and this 50-yard strike added another layer to their attack. The final score against the Falcons was 35-13, and the deep ball was a major reason for that blowout win.

item.title: Four Former Tigers Land on the 2027 Hall of Fame Ballot
item.description: The Baseball Hall of Fame released its 2027 BBWAA ballot on Monday, and four former Detroit Tigers are on it: outfielder Torii Hunter and pitchers Andrew Miller , Francisco Rodríguez and Joakim Soria . Twenty-seven players are on the ballot, 14 of them for the first time. Hunter played for Detroit in 2013 and 2014, Soria in 2014 and 2015, Rodríguez in 2016 and 2017, and Miller began his career with the Tigers in 2006 and 2007 after they drafted him sixth overall. Ballots are due Dec. 31, and the results are announced Jan. 19 at 6 p.m. ET on MLB Network. Jul 11, 2026; Minneapolis, Minnesota, USA; Minnesota Twins play-by-play announcer Dick Bremer is reflected in the glasses of Torii Hunter as he delivers his Minnesota Twins Hall of Fame induction speech at Target Field. Mandatory Credit: Matt Blewett-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Where the Tigers on the Hall of Fame Ballot Stand Rodríguez and Hunter are the only two of the four who have been voted on before. Rodríguez finished 15th in the 2026 voting at 11.8% of the vote , and Hunter finished 16th at 8.7%. A candidate needs 75% of the ballots cast to be elected, so both have a long way to climb. Miller and Soria are newcomers and have never appeared on a ballot. It is going to be very hard for any of the former Tigers players to get into the hall of fame in 2027. Torii Hunter Is Running Out of Chances A player stays on the ballot for a maximum of 10 elections, and only as long as he keeps drawing at least 5% of the vote. This will be Hunter’s seventh time on the ballot and Rodríguez’s fifth, so Rodríguez has the longer runway of the two. Even if neither gets in this year, they still have a few more chances. The former Tigers players may have to wait another year or two to make it into Cooperstown, New York. Buster Posey Leads a Crowded 2027 Class San Francisco Giants catcher Buster Posey is on the ballot for the first time. It would be hard to believe that Posey would not get in on the first ballot. Carlos Beltrán and Andruw Jones were the only two players elected in the 2026 balloting, so there is a chance that more get in this time. Chase Utley, Andy Pettitte, Félix Hernández and Alex Rodriguez all return after finishing third, fourth, fifth and sixth a year ago, at 59.1%, 48.5%, 46.1% and 40% of the vote. It would not be a surprise to see them make it into the hall of fame in 2027. There is no limit on how many players can be elected in a single year. The limit is on the voters: an elector may name no more than 10 candidates on a ballot. So if Posey, Utley, Pettitte, Hernández and Rodriguez all cleared 75% in 2027, there would be nothing stopping a sixth or a seventh from getting in with them.

item.description: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images The Kansas City Chiefs proved they can win big games without their full starting lineup. Patrick Mahomes threw five touchdown passes in a 35-13 victory over the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday. This win moved the team to 7-2 on the season. The real story was not just the score, but who caught the balls. Young players and backups stepped up to make plays when the stars got hurt. This depth gives the Chiefs a strong chance to keep winning as the season goes on. Patrick Mahomes showed he is still the best quarterback in the game. He finished with 348 passing yards and a 135.5 passer rating. That rating is the sixth-best of his 10-year career. It was his first game with five touchdowns since 2022. The Chiefs won without their leading rusher Kenneth Walker III. Three starting offensive linemen were absent for the majority of the contest. Mahomes was “a little nervous” about his throwing elbow after an injury last week. Young Players Step Into the Spotlight The success of this team relies on new faces making big plays. Two of the five touchdown catches came from players scoring their first NFL touchdown. Mahomes made sure to find the game ball for them after the game. item.title: Wales' pre-match haka light show was a 'military operation' a year in the making
item.description: Wales watching New Zealand perform the haka ahead of Saturday's victory [Getty Images] The light show that wowed crowds ahead of Wales' win against New Zealand was a year in the making, according to a Principality Stadium boss. During the All Blacks' pre-match haka on Saturday, Wales' players were bathed in red light and smoke. Staring down their opponents, the dramatic scene set the tone for their defiant performance and historic victory. Alex Luff, head of event sales and operations at the Principality Stadium, said the focus of the display was to represent Wales' response to the challenge that New Zealand were going to lay down. "It all started 12 months ago, after the Wales-New Zealand game last November, where we delivered the haka in a new, theatrical way," he said. "But that was all about the haka. So, 12 months on, we wanted to focus on the team's response, Wales' response." The idea for the display came following last year's match against New Zealand [Reuters] Explaining how the concept came together, Luff added: "It's very much a team effort. "From the band and the choir to the pyrotechnics that we have, all of this has to be layered to minute detail to deliver that spectacle. "It's like a military operation. Everything is down to the minute, even to the second." He said that, after the national anthems, organisers had a minute-and-a-half to get 150 choristers, 50 military band members and 50 members of the display team off the pitch and then "bring all the production on" to prepare for the haka. Behind the scenes of Wales' red light display [Welsh Rugby Union] Wales went on to celebrate their first victory against New Zealand in 73 years, sparking euphoric scenes in Cardiff and across the country. Steve Tandy's side broke their 34-match losing sequence against the All Blacks that stretched back to 1953. Luff said he hoped his team's pre-match display lived as long in people's memories as the result on the pitch. "[The reaction] has been extraordinary. I think it's really demonstrated what Welsh rugby and the Principality Stadium is all about," he said. item.description: David Richard-Imagn Images Kyrie Irving will not play in Sunday’s matchup against the Boston Celtics, leaving the Dallas Mavericks to fight without their star guard.
